# Uncovered 3: resource-paid weapon damage

This batch adds a real resource-spending damage model. The initial-ID total stays at 216 closed, 5,244 uncovered and 0 regressions; it does not claim a new original-ID closure. One formerly informational Staff of Striking sentence now has computed support: covered is 7,918, info 23,620 and allow remains 0. Work continues after this checkpoint.

Staff of Striking, Staff of Thunder and Lightning, Staff of Withering and Staff of Power now use their explicitly stated Quarterstaff profile. Previously these Staff-category inventory rows produced no weapon attack. Their native weapon die is 1d6 Bludgeoning; attuned potency is +3 for Striking and +2 for Thunder/Power, with effective eligibility still required. Withering receives its physical weapon profile only.

Striking's optional hit rider spends 1–3 of its own ten charges and rolls 1d6 Force per charge. Thunder's optional Lightning hit rider spends only its own once-per-dawn Lightning resource and rolls 2d6 Lightning. Thunder, combined Thunder and Lightning, Lightning Strike and Thunderclap retain their independent counters. Their retained LU payload/order is unchanged. The old advisory Lightning rider is replaced by an actual paid roll rather than automatically included in every weapon's damage. Normal weapon damage is unchanged by opening the resource panel or having charges available. Polearm Master's Pole Strike keeps its own 1d4 Bludgeoning die and inherits its actual staff's resource binding, including two different wielded staffs.

The pure `atkSpendDice` schema validates literal dice, a canonical damage type, positive integer costs, per-charge scaling and exact charge/daily-use bindings. The sheet handler scopes output to an eligible source and current pool. The UI rechecks character, source, effective attunement, equip/quantity, resource identity and affordability immediately before spending; it uses the existing undo/save/resource operations. A critical hit doubles dice once while keeping the same cost. Spending is committed once; a second click cannot spend again, closing does not refund, and a last-charge result can still finish. Reload preserves expenditure. Target HP is never changed by this damage roll.

Native resources now carry derived inventory indices and inventory rows carry their finalized charge keys. Binding occurs after `keepResKeys`, which can preserve/rename a key. This changes output metadata only: builder inputs and storage keys remain unchanged. Existing name/occurrence keys are retained, so permanent per-copy identity across removal/reordering of duplicate items remains a separate migration task.

Thunder's retained LU and new paid rider are consolidated in fx-Z8; its obsolete L5/Z1 overlap exception was removed. Explicit base metadata preserves each item's raw effects. Source prose is unchanged. Staff of Power's 2014-only Power Strike is not invented for 2024. Last-charge destruction/conversion, Withering's save/disadvantage consequence, and Thunder's other damage/save consequences remain outside this model and receive no new computed claim.

The clause gate recognizes executed paid dice and resource prices as separate values. A one-use cost cannot explain a one-minute condition. Its strict initial-ID comparison remains 0 regressions. The Lightbringer test warmup now installs the actual case's packs and refreshes the real cross-reference index synchronously, restoring the original builder afterward; strict raw HTML comparison remains enabled. No allowlist/classification rule was relaxed.

# Uncovered 3: critical dice and separate attack self damage

This batch closes 10 more original sentence IDs: 216 closed in total, 5,244 uncovered, and 0 regressed IDs. Covered is 7,917, info remains 23,621, allow remains 0. Work continues after this checkpoint.

Scourge of Shadow now computes its +3/3d4 weapon damage while wielded, including without attunement, and its extra 4d4 Necrotic only against a Good creature. Its critical attack upgrades the base to 3d6 and the Good-target rider to 4d6 before ordinary critical doubling: the actual critical roll is 6d6 plus the unchanged flat modifier, with 8d6 Necrotic against a Good creature. A natural 18 is recognized as critical. Unknown alignment, an Object, or a non-Good creature grants no Good-target rider.

An unattuned wielder has a separate self-damage resolve control, including after an attack that missed. It rolls 2d4 normally or 2d6 after a critical attack. This separate self damage is not doubled again and is never mixed into damage to the target. Opening the panel or rolling changes no HP. Apply uses the existing damage operation exactly once, including temporary HP absorption, concentration/death-save handling, undo and save. It applies the full amount despite resistance/immunity, as the explicit source policy requires. A character change, stowing the source or attuning it invalidates an open resolve panel.

The ten closures are the +3/3d4 weapon clause, Good-target 4d4, unattuned self damage/bypass, critical base upgrade, and critical Necrotic die-face upgrade, each in the DMG and CoA copies. Source prose is unchanged. Initiative already added Charisma to Dexterity correctly; no replacement initiative model was introduced. The explicit while-attuned Fast Reflexes benefit now retains its lifetime when stowed, and the existing attack-ability mechanism chooses Charisma when higher than the Whip's Strength/Dexterity options. The existing Veil resistance gate remains used-and-attuned; the malformed lighting clause is still unresolved.

- Nested `dieReplace[].critD` and opt-in `atkDice[].critD` validate literal normal/critical dice. They produce optional critical expressions in typed packets. Die faces are selected consistently before random/3D rolls and result aggregation; flat bonuses are unchanged. Critical result/history expressions show the actual doubled dice. Ordinary packet shape and explicit manual damage overrides remain compatible. A later winning base-die replacement clears a stale critical override.
- `atkSelfDamage` is a declared FX field with a source-scoped handler and strict normal/critical/type/bypass schema. Output metadata and temporary popup state introduce no builder input change or storage-key rename. The UI rechecks owner, source and effective inventory state; the existing HP operation avoids a second damage/temporary-HP implementation.
- Scourge keeps the Whip's native Slashing type without redundantly forcing it after class overrides. The 2024 Pact of the Blade's Necrotic/Psychic/Radiant choice therefore survives, including while unattuned; its Good-target rider remains fixed Necrotic.
- Scourge's six GX entries are consolidated in fx-M1. Loader evidence confirms identical payload and entry order after relocation. The obsolete cross-file overlap exemption was removed rather than expanded. Static unattuned potency stays in the separate FXO metadata table.
- The custom resolve panel owns its roll controls, preventing the prior attack's generic d20 bar from being inserted. Its input and controls were visually checked at both viewports.

The gate now recognizes the actual self-damage field and its explicit defense-bypass policy. New critical fields provide separate normal/critical amounts, like existing multi-part charge fields, and the literal die-face representation for an explicit upgrade. Six synthetic checks cover independent amounts, bare die faces, missing upgrades, supported bypass and removal of the computed record. No status rule or allowlist was relaxed; unsupported/missing upgrades receive no computed credit.

# Uncovered 3: independent attunement and weapon definitions

This batch closes 6 more original sentence IDs: 202 closed in total, 5,258 uncovered, and 0 regressed IDs. Covered is 7,902; info remains 23,622 and allow remains 0. Work continues after this checkpoint.

The six closures are Hazirawn's unattuned +1 attack/damage and extra 1d6 Necrotic (DMG and misc14 copies), plus Ruby Rod of Asmodeus's Necrotic conversion and +2d12 against a Good creature (DMG and CoA copies). The source rule prose is unchanged. Unknown alignment, an Object, or a non-Good creature grants no Ruby Rod rider.

- Inventory now stores an optional `attuned` boolean independently from `eq`. Explicit booleans survive normalization, import, save, reload, and putting an item away. Legacy requiring-attunement rows inherit their old use/equip state once. The existing v3 input format and storage keys are retained; this is an explicit optional-field migration, not an undocumented shape change.
- One allocator supplies effective attunement to item effects, actions, weapon/armor/shield potency, item spells, and exported inventory. It checks stock, eligibility, canonical duplicates, prerequisites, and slot limits, including expanded limits. Stowing an attuned item retains its slot; ending attunement releases it. Quantity zero grants no attack or magic effect, and import preserves zero rather than resurrecting consumed stock.
- Sheet and builder inventory expose separate use/equip and attunement controls. Failed requests explain the class/prerequisite, duplicate, stock or slot issue. Legacy invalid requests remain visible with their inactive reason. Ownership is checked before changing the saved builder. The sheet's existing manual-edit guard remains in place. PDF labels use effective attunement independently of wearing.
- `ITEM_OVERRIDE_FIELDS` validates static item metadata separately from FX entries: base definitions, an explicitly retained unattuned flat weapon bonus, and attunement-required energy weapons. Wand of Orcus uses a Mace and Ruby Rod a Morningstar, so normal weapon proficiency and attack derivation apply. An unattuned Sun Blade or Duskcrusher hilt does not create an ordinary weapon attack. Activation timing remains a separate open mechanic.
- Hazirawn computes +1/1d6 when wielded without active attunement and +2/2d6 while attuned and used. Its two mutually exclusive source lifetimes do not stack. Its dice, and Wand of Orcus's existing 2d12, now participate in typed normal/critical damage rolls. Ruby Rod changes its base damage to Necrotic and adds the target-qualified rolled packet.
- A Cleric no longer receives Staff of the Magi item spells despite failing its attunement class requirement. A qualified Wizard still receives them. This fixes an existing item-spell path that bypassed the central eligibility check.

The new static metadata exposed a clause-gate mismatch: any FXO object without `fx` was treated as an explicit `fx:null`, incorrectly moving sentences to info. The engine preserves row effects when the property is absent. The gate now mirrors that behavior, with three synthetic checks for metadata-only, explicit null, and replacement overrides. Its atom for `unattunedBonus` describes the actual attack/damage scalar tested by U22. The temporary false info credit was rejected; the final info count is unchanged.

# Uncovered 3: target-qualified weapon damage

The new attack-target model computes conditional weapon bonuses and rolls verified extra damage by type. This batch closes 13 additional rule sentences: 196 closed since the initial 5,460, leaving 5,264. Work continues on the remaining rules; this is a checkpoint, not a completion claim.

## Mechanical behavior

- The sheet stores an optional current target: creature type (or Object/Structure), alignment, current/max HP, and explicit source-qualified tags. Unknown facts do not satisfy a condition. Old saved states migrate to Unknown without renaming a storage key; unrecognized future target properties survive normalization.
- A typed `target` predicate gates the entry before sheet derivation. An inactive entry retains only source/control metadata, so the controls remain available without granting its effects. A third optional argument to `__bldSheetFor` supplies isolated target context for tests.
- `atkDice.roll:true` opts a verified rider into actual damage calculation and rolling. Legacy conditional prose is not interpreted as unconditional dice. The calculator groups base damage and riders by damage type, retains their sources, and clamps each type at zero. Critical damage doubles dice, including riders, and leaves flat modifiers unchanged.
- The real damage buttons, roll history, manual-roll type label, calculation breakdown, and PDF weapon model preserve mixed damage types. Explicit custom damage overrides still replace the calculated total. Long mixed expressions wrap in the mobile damage column.
- Existing typed critical thresholds now reach attack rolls: a natural 19 can be marked critical without being mislabeled Natural 20.

It cannot add atoms or broaden existing restrictions. U19 proves the actual Strength modifier, minimum +1 and retained Performance proficiency. `Rocker#3` remains uncovered, while `Rocker#4` correctly closes. The three additional closures are therefore real adjacent benefits, not the rejected Instrument Weapon claim.

## Open readings and limitations

Pluvenn Grappleclaws combines Athletics climbing Advantage with Advantage on an Unarmed Strike used to Grapple. The app's 2024 Grapple uses the target's save, leaving no attacker roll for that Advantage. No invented target-save Disadvantage or half-implemented compound closure is added.

Necronomicon's Voidmarked social Advantage has no explicit ending condition after attunement loss or inventory removal. Both copies remain uncovered. Its existing once-only ability-score lifecycle issue is recorded in requests.md and is not silently migrated to the company-training model. These readings are also marked reading not decided in rules-notes.md.

Piety, charm expiry, marked/metal targets, state durations and shape-change selection changes remain player tracked. The Gamma switch supplies only its stated spell-save benefit, Promotion only Martial Training and Metamorphosis only Darkvision. Other clauses of those features remain open. All 5,277 remaining uncovered clauses remain visible, with no claim that the task's full rule universe is complete.

The four reserved sheet bugs remain unchanged: Gloom Stalker 2014 Iron Mind, Ranger 6 Roving in 2014, Draconic Bloodline 2014 level and Attack action text "per Extra Attack".

## New mechanical model

`consume:{duration}` separates an activated item's lifetime from its inventory row. Drinking spends one bottle. The effect persists at quantity zero, after removing the inventory row, after Apply and after reload. End removes the benefit without restoring stock. Two bottles do not double it. The same switch cannot consume again while active. The player may End and Drink again to refresh the effect. Durations are displayed and ended manually, with no wall-clock expiry claim.

The speed panel now renders GX `C.moves` alongside legacy `C.speeds`, retaining the greatest displayed speed per mode after conditions and Exhaustion. It does not sum duplicate flight grants or mutate the sheet data. The missing live display was found during visual review and corrected, with dedicated UI comparisons.

The model reuses `S.fxT` booleans and existing inventory quantities. No storage key or builder/play-state input format changes. Optional computed metadata inside the existing `C.fxToggles` list describes Drink and End controls. The item source deliberately excludes `consume` entries, preventing duplicate effects when the bottle is equipped. The new independent source discovers available or active effects. The schema requires an inactive default and a duration label. The gate uses that duration only to explain numbers attached to a real typed benefit. Duration alone cannot create a movement atom, covered by positive and negative selftests.

| Potion | Computed active benefit | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Climbing | Climb equals current Speed, qualified Athletics Advantage | 1 hour |
| Flying | Fly equals current Speed, hover and end-of-flight falling instructions | 1 hour |
| Invulnerability | Resistance to all thirteen standard damage types | 1 minute |
| Giant Strength, cloud | STR becomes 27 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Giant Strength, fire | STR becomes 25 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Giant Strength, frost | STR becomes 23 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Giant Strength, hill | STR becomes 21 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Giant Strength, stone | STR becomes 23 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Giant Strength, storm | STR becomes 29 only if lower | 1 hour |
| Pugilism | Every Unarmed Strike hit adds 1d6 Force, other weapons do not | 10 minutes |

The amounts and durations were reread from the app's own DMGI item sentences. No book verification is claimed. Independent-lifetime behavior does not interpret arbitrary spell names or implement the remaining target, transformation and action-economy models.

Twenty-seven additional native clauses receive code atoms with paired record/selection-removal tests. These include eight legacy cleric grants, eight subclass advantage notes, five fixed skill grants, Warden's selected save, Battlecaster's selected weapon, Woodwise's selected skill, Syndicate Spy's Forgery Kit and the two spell-attack Advantage sentences. Native benefits receive no duplicate data effect. White Necromancer's difference removes both existing skill sources, preserving unrelated spells and advantage rules. Eight additional legacy level-1 cases independently verify the source level instead of inheriting the merged feature-row level.

## Implemented behavior

`fx-Z5.js` adds six initial subclass state entries, nineteen advantage entries, five feat entries, three item entries and the ranged-weapon feat entry. Piloting uses the existing extra-skill registry. The new `weaponGroups` field grants only matching weapon categories/kinds. Thrown melee weapons do not accidentally become ranged weapons. `classOnly` prevents Alchemist Hyperelastic from leaking to the unrelated Artificer Mutagenist subclass, including in multiclass builds. Each field's implementation is under 60 added lines.

WXS resistance, immunity, skill and sense records are recognized only for the matching source feature and level and complete literal rule sentences. Twenty-one native feat code atoms have paired tests. Existing computed benefits do not receive duplicate effects.

Mythallar Cloak retains the existing 10-charge pool and attunement requirement, and grants Fly 30, hover instructions and one 1d4 Radiant rider while active. Ring of Spacewalking and Spacewalkers grant flight only in zero gravity. Source item rows enforce attunement. The schema field `attune` increases the attunement limit and is not a flag meaning an item requires attunement, so these entries must not set it to 1.

# Uncovered 3: Phase 1, conservative classification

Branch `codex/uncovered-3`, base `f6d77cb1b52289f21ae33775a532effdae764d18`. `git fetch origin` completed. The remote fetch refspec initially exposed only main, so the required branch was fetched explicitly. `git branch -r --contains f6d77cb1` lists only `origin/claude/uncovered-1`. Worktree: `/workspace/work/uncovered-3`. No PR and no main push.

This checkpoint changes this report only. The application and gate statuses do not change. The owner requested a stop, commit and push at each phase boundary. Phase 2 has not started.

## Scope and confidence

Every one of the 5,460 baseline IDs is assigned below, with its text hash, full gate sentence and reason. The ID/hash set is checked for exact equality with the tracked baseline. G1 is an existing-model capacity classification, not proof of a missing effect. Before adding an effect, inspect the complete feature, existing GX/FXO and code handlers, edition, level, attunement and choices. Existing computed behavior requires a code atom and a difference test, never another additive effect.

The first pass used narrow whole-sentence patterns for resistance, immunity, proficiency, advantage, movement and senses. All 182 initial G1 candidates were read, and 15 were moved back to G3 for compound behavior, card lifecycle or protected owner decisions. The final G1 count is 167. The remainder was conservatively assigned to G3 under the explicit instruction to put unplaced sentences there. These 5,283 rows are NOT a finding that 5,283 sentences require a new model. Most remain unplaced, with that limitation stated in each reason. This is a conservative initial triage, not a completed engineering analysis of every remaining feature.

G2 has zero confirmed members. A schema extension is not established merely because a keyword lacks an atom. No under-60-line implementation has been proven necessary and sufficient in this report. Therefore ten G2 examples cannot be supplied honestly. Revisit unresolved G3 candidates before treating this as a complete G1/G2 implementation backlog. G1, G3 and G4 each have ten real examples below. No synthetic examples stand in for source sentences.

G4 records are semantic reason-code candidates. The existing gate may reject those codes because its other guards or the surrounding numeric atoms do not match. No info label, allowlist, reason code or gate condition was added. In particular, the proposed FORM:TABLE reasons do not authorize relabeling slot or charge rules.

## Differences between brief and actual code or environment

- README.md does not exist in this worktree and was skipped as instructed. No books directory was used.
- The schema and handlers support more than the brief lists. `mv` accepts `speed`, `speed2`, `speedHalf` and numeric mode speeds. The schema already includes `saveProf`, `slotAdd`, `dieStep`, `attackRow` and other later-engine fields. Do not create new fields for these behaviors.
- `advOn` and `atkDice` do not universally automate a dice roller. `defFx` writes advantage notes, and the late attack handler writes rider dice and notes. A G1 classification means the existing representation is available, not that every play decision is computed.
- System Python has Playwright, but its expected bundled Chromium is absent. `python3 -m playwright install chromium` failed with HTTP 403 `Domain forbidden` at cdn.playwright.dev. System `/usr/bin/chromium` exists. It blocks file navigation with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR. Tests ran successfully using a temporary external `sitecustomize.py` that selects system Chromium and maps only this checkout's file URLs to a loopback HTTP server. No repo test was edited. The exact test prefix was `PYTHONPATH=/workspace/work/runtime`.
- `tools/build/node_modules` was missing in the new worktree. `npm ci` installed 90 packages. `build.py` reproduced the tracked artifacts exactly, so neither generated file needs a commit.
